newsitem.title: UK: Local taxes set to rise after UK budget - Labour.
newsitem.headline: Local taxes set to rise after UK budget - Labour.

text.p: Britons will more than pay for the one penny in the pound income tax cut in Tuesday's budget in the form of increased local council taxes, the main opposition Labour Party said on Wednesday.

Environment spokesman Frank Dobson said council tax would have to rise by six percent next year and by more in subsequent years to make up for cuts in government grants to local authorities revealed in budget papers.
He told a news conference this would cost the average family 40 stg next year and 200 stg over the next three years.

"(Chancellor of the Exchequer) Kenneth Clarke publicly claims credit for reducing the standard rate of income tax by 1p while other figures slipped out by the government show that council tax is set to rise by the equivalent of putting an extra 2p onto the standard rate of income tax," Dobson said.

Dobson was speaking after Labour unveiled a new poster claiming that the average family was paying 2,120 stg a year more in taxes than at the 1992 general election. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
